content: If you suspect an overdose and the individual is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, kidney function assessments, and eye examinations. These tests help monitor your condition and ensure the medication is working safely. Be sure to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The liquid form of this medication should be stored in the refrigerator but must not be frozen. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Valganciclovir is converted into ganciclovir in the body. Ganciclovir can suppress bone marrow function, which may result in a significant reduction in blood cell counts, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. This effect can lead to anemia, a weakened immune response to infections, and an increased risk of bleeding. Your doctor will monitor your blood test results and adjust your treatment to minimize these risks. Ganciclovir may impair fertility in both men and women and can harm an unborn baby. It has been shown to cause tumors in laboratory animals, and while there is no direct evidence in humans, valganciclovir should be considered potentially carcinogenic. Discuss the risks and benefits of this medication with your doctor. Valganciclovir is an antiviral medication that is converted in the body to its active form, ganciclovir. It is used to prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease in individuals who have undergone organ transplants. CMV disease can cause severe infections, including CMV retinitis, an eye infection that can lead to blindness. Valganciclovir works by slowing the growth of the CMV virus. It is also used to treat CMV retinitis in individuals with advanced HIV disease (AIDS). However, valganciclovir is not a cure for CMV disease, and some individuals may experience worsening of CMV retinitis despite treatment. Before starting valganciclovir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth with food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. Swallow the tablets whole. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using the provided measuring device. Wash your hands thoroughly after handling this medication. Avoid contact with broken or crushed tablets, the liquid form, or the dust from the tablets on your skin, mucous membranes, or eyes. If contact occurs, wash the area thoroughly with soap and water. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition. For children, the dosage is also based on body size. To achieve the best results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals to maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body. Continue taking it exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not change your dose or stop taking it without consulting your doctor, even for a short time. Do not substitute ganciclovir for valganciclovir without medical advice. Common side effects may include diarrhea, upset stomach, dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness, or tremors. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking valganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, ganciclovir, or acyclovir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Valganciclovir may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are taking valganciclovir before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. To prevent pregnancy, men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during all sexual activity while on treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. Women of childbearing age should use reliable forms of birth control (e.g., birth control pills and condoms) during treatment and for at least 30 days after stopping the medication. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to the potential risk to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may decrease bone marrow function or lower blood cell counts (e.g., cancer chemotherapy, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, zidovudine) or cause kidney problems (e.g., cyclosporine). Valganciclovir is very similar to ganciclovir; do not use ganciclovir while taking valganciclovir unless directed by your doctor.
